priorStories.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula advance to runoff
priorStories.body:
Brazil’s electoral court said Flávio Bolsonaro received 47.03% of valid votes and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva received 45.16%, with 99.99% of ballots counted.

Neither secured a majority, sending them to a presidential runoff on October 25.

priorStories.headline: Germany adds €1 billion in Ukraine military aid
priorStories.body:
Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced €1 billion in additional military aid for Ukraine and €350 million to repair its energy system during a visit to Kyiv.

German executives also signed 14 agreements with Ukrainian government and business counterparts worth about €6.6 billion. They include agreements involving IRIS-T missiles, radar equipment and interceptors for jet-powered drones. A broader defense-production agreement remains under negotiation.

priorStories.headline: Yemen’s government launches offensive against Houthis
priorStories.body:
The head of Yemen’s Saudi-backed Presidential Leadership Council announced military operations intended to retake Houthi-controlled territory and extend government authority nationwide.

Government-aligned forces said they were striking Houthi targets in Sanaa and Saada. Houthi-run media attributed an attack on Sanaa to Saudi Arabia, but Saudi officials had not confirmed that account. No territorial gains were reported in the initial accounts.

candidates.summary: The Nobel Assembly awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. Hegemann and Nagel discovered the light-sensitive protein channelrhodopsin, and Deisseroth developed its use as a light-controlled switch for nerve cells.
candidates.title: Optogenetics researchers win Nobel medicine prize

candidates.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced that an extraordinary cabinet meeting would be called to dissolve parliament and schedule a general election for November 29. Sánchez said a renewed mandate was needed after repeated parliamentary deadlock, including the rejection of government housing measures.
candidates.title: Spain calls early general election for November 29

candidates.summary: Norway’s government said it would submit legislation proposing a temporary ban on AI-equipped glasses in selected public and privacy-sensitive locations. Possible locations include schools, parks, museums, public events, medical facilities and changing rooms. The proposal is not yet law, and the government said private use and some other uses would remain permitted.
candidates.title: Norway proposes temporary restrictions on AI glasses

candidates.summary: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces seized key positions and large parts of Dhubab district overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to three military sources and one government source cited by Reuters. Houthi-aligned media denied that government forces had advanced. The reported gains followed the government’s October 4 announcement of a nationwide offensive.
candidates.title: Yemeni government forces report gains near Bab el-Mandeb

candidates.summary: Odesa regional governor Oleh Kiper said Russian airstrikes targeted industrial and port infrastructure in southern Ukraine and that resulting fires had been extinguished. Russia’s Defense Ministry separately claimed it struck fuel storage facilities and two cargo vessels carrying military equipment or supplies. Those Russian claims were not independently verified in the initial reports.
candidates.title: Russian strikes target Odesa region ports and industry

candidates.summary: Thailand’s Interior Ministry said the death toll from flooding that began September 16 had risen to 31.
candidates.title: Thailand flood death toll rises to 31
